dod_intent_evidence: DoD intent is genuine and passes the gate — Air Force SBIR Phase II 2023, 'Space Based Sensors for Safety and Situational Awareness for Future ISAM Vehicle Rendezvous' ($1,680,508), plus a GlobeNewswire release on a PSIONIC collaboration 'Supporting RPOD, Space Control, and Space Battle Management for U.S. Space Force and SDA Missions' (2026-02-11). The pack fails the evidence-sufficiency gate, not the intent gate.
score_evidence: Own-language word count is ~492, below the ~500-word floor, and roughly half of that is two leadership bios and an office address

The entire product portfolio is four code names with no description: 'Perception (THOR) / Simulation (ASGARD) / Intelligence (HEIMDALL) / Autonomy (ODIN)' — deployment topics cannot be scored as absent when the product is never described in enough detail for them to arise

The only capability language is abstract vision copy — 'Our work extends to edge-based decision support, coordinated maneuver planning, resilient command and control, and secure integration across sensing and navigation architectures' — which nods at edge and resilience without describing any system
what_they_do: Nine-person Sausalito company building space-object characterization, simulation, and autonomy software for space domain awareness, rendezvous/proximity operations, and space control.
